items.p: Hi! I'm Yash. I am in the 10th grade at Round Rock High School. I have a passion for Computer Science and Engineering. Mostly, I love to figure out why something works or why it doesn't. I'm also curious about how to make it better. On weekends, I'm usually hanging out with my friends, playing pickleball or at the pool. My course goals are to figure out how to configure VEX robots and how to make them efficiently. I would love to work more with motors and coding robots to accomplish different things.

Project Description: For this project, we got to choose from a variety of simple machines, and we had to build one and find out its IMA, AMA, and more. We had to find out the IMA and AMA for every simple machine assigned for our class. As well, we also had to create sketches and find real-world examples for every machine. In the project, we had criteria for reaching a certain IMA and AMA, and also the size.

Reflection: In the project, originally, we misinterpreted how high we needed the lever to be positioned on the fulcrum. This affected how much weight we could lift. Also, we had to find out where to position the weight to get maximum efficiency. This project helped me develop my problem-solving skills by determining how to position the lever to get full effort.

Description: For this project, we had to create a compound machine containing three different machines that all worked together to accomplish our goal. For the goal, we had to lift a 1kg weight 6 inches off the ground using 3 different machines. Another requirement was that we had to use only VEX parts. Also we had to have an IMA of close to, or around, 5.

Reflection: In retrospect, our original design wasn't possible. That is why we changed the design to lift the wheel and axle off the ground, and the lever as well. However, in the middle, besides a block-and-tackle pulley, we used a fixed pulley so the thread could run under it and latch to the first-class lever. These changes helped us understand how compound machines interact with each other better, and since one machine was too high or too low, the entire machine wouldn't work.

Project Description: We have been hired by Castles R Us Toy Design Company to create an unique model castle to be marketed as a childrens toy. We must design a castle to contain a list of architectural elements and a solid motte to support our castle. We must also include several bonus designs to overall boost the design of the castle while also incorperating all different inventor tools.

What I learned: I learned many different new inventor tools like mirror and pattern which eased the process of making my castle. I also learned how to find out solutions when the answer was not given to us, I had to find new videos and new ideas to solve my problem. I learned how to sketch a whole castle and turrets, also I learned how to make new planes on different axis's to make things appear on new surfaces. I learned how to use the loft feature and revolve feature to make tops of turrets

The project required us to make a launcher from rubber bands paper clips and popsicle sticks. We had to record data and launch a cotton ball with our device.

Reverse engineering is basically dismantling a product so as to find out how it was made and what is its working principle. An engineer researches the materials, components, and mechanisms in a product to figure out how the pieces fit and work together. Here I reverse engineered a wind, up toy in order to figure out its mechanical system. This process allowed me to realize that even very simple things need thoughtful planning and design.

Visual analysis is a primary assessment of a product's look through elements and principles of design like color, shape, balance, and proportion. The mechanical toy visually illustrates an effective decision of design elements where vibrant hues, soft and gentle curves, along with a shinny surface are used to lure kids and hence increase its commercial potential. The usage of oval shapes in fact is a sign of safety and friendliness to the intended users. Through this exercise, I discovered that the looks of a product are of utmost importance in both attractive and marketing a product.

Functional analysis looks into the working of a product by breaking down its inputs, processes, and outputs. In the case of a wind, up toy, turning the key stores mechanical energy in a spring, which is later passed through gears to create movement. The input is the force used to wind the toy, and the output is motion. I learned how energy is stored and converted in simple mechanical systems.
Presentation:

Structural analysis is the process of dissecting a product to examine its parts and understand the way they are assembled. Through my disassembling of the wind, up toy, I discovered a metal spring, plastic gears, a shaft, and a protective outer casing. Each component is essential for enabling the movement and shielding the internal mechanism. The exercise gave me a clearer insight into how the structure of a product is directly related to its function.

By reverse engineering, I got to know that product design, functionality, and structure are all elements that interact visually. I realized that a wind-up toy is packed with a system of gears and a spring that stores and produces mechanical energy. I found it fascinating how every single component, no matter how small, has a crucial part in the toy's movement. Besides, the whole endeavor gave me a deeper insight into mechanical systems and sharpened my problem, solving and observation skills.

The trammel toy invocated many skills, mainly this project worked with assembly and all of the parts inside of it. This project helped me learn to create new pieces while inside the assemly mode like hardware and also this project taught me exploded views in the drawing files.
